title: rewrite-lint-entrypoint-and-introduce-dep-staleness-check
author: Jordan Kim
description:
Motivation: Our lint and formatting jobs have drifted into multiple ad-hoc entrypoints (JS, Python, docs), causing duplicated setup and flakey caches. This PR centralizes the lint entrypoint, standardizes environment setup across runners, and adds a lightweight dep-staleness CI check to proactively surface out-of-sync lockfiles and requirement pin drift.

What this PR does (summary):
- Introduces .github/workflows/lint-orchestrator.yml: a single workflow that dispatches language-specific jobs (node, python, md) with consistent bootstrap steps and cache keys.
- Adds tools/ci/lint-entrypoint.sh: unified bash entrypoint used by all lint jobs; loads environment variables, prepares venv/node_modules, and invokes the language-specific linters.
- Adds scripts/check-dep-staleness.py: a small, fast script that verifies lockfiles (yarn.lock, poetry.lock, requirements.txt) are in sync with manifests; exits non-zero when drift is detected and prints actionable remediation commands.
- Bumps dev deps: eslint@8.55.0, prettier@2.9.0 (minor bumps kept intentionally minimal), poetry-core pinned to 1.6.x in CI to avoid transient resolver differences.
- Removes duplicate CI steps from legacy workflows and replaces them with references to the new orchestrator via workflow_call.
- Update README/CONTRIBUTING with quick instructions for running the unified lint locally and resolving lockfile drift.

Checklist: 
- [x] Centralize lint orchestration and remove duplicated setup steps
- [x] Add dep-staleness CI job with clear error output
- [x] Keep dev dependency bumps conservative and opt-in for runtime dependencies
- [x] Add docs for contributors and CI troubleshooting

Why this approach: consolidating the entrypoint reduces maintenance burden and standardizes cache key logic which was a major source of flakiness. The dep-staleness check is intentionally lightweight (no full dependency resolution) and acts as an early-warning to avoid post-merge grind where lockfiles are out of sync across language stacks. Linear: ENG-4981 tracked the lint flakiness; ENG-5013 requested lockfile checks for cross-team stability.

Notes for reviewers: The shell entrypoint contains guardrails for CI (fast-fail on missing interpreters, clear hints for fix commands). The python script is pure stdlib except for typing and runs on GitHub's Ubuntu images. If you want a separate action later we can extract the script into a composite action, but keeping it in-repo keeps iteration fast.

Release impact: None on runtime code. This is CI/tooling only.

Related: references to prior CI cleanups (see ENG-3720 and pr-71220) for historical context.
